newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end near day's lows.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end near day's lows.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Thursday in a fairly active session, undermined by weaker physical prices and 10-15 day forecasts calling for mostly above-normal weather.
March slipped 9.4 cents to close at $1.922 per million British thermal units. April settled 9.3 cents lower at $1.911. Other months ended down by 1.1 to 7.4 cents.

"It's a tough call from here. These levels are starting to look pretty attractive, but the weather's not very supportive," said one East Coast industrial source, adding there could be more selling pressure ahead.

Despite a brief cold snap later this week, few expected much upside near-term, particularly with eastern storage running about 50 percent above year-ago and very mild weather forecast for later this month and into early March.
"Eastern LDCs (utilities) are not returning phone calls. They have too much inventory and they know the gas will be out there if they need it," said a Houston-based marketer.

Technical traders again saw March support at Tuesday's low of $1.85 and then at the contract low of $1.749. Resistance was seen at $2.08-2.09 and then $2.25-2.30. Looking at April, support was pegged at $1.87 and then at $1.845, with additional buying likely at the contract low of $1.701. April resistance was seen at $2.04 and then at $2.16.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices eased slightly Thursday to the high-$1.80s to $1.90 area. Midcon pipes lost similar ground to the low-$1.70s. New York city gate gas also was talked modestly lower at $2.15.
The 12-month strip fell 4.2 cents to $2.052. NYMEX said an estimated 57,943 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 46,222.
NYMEX March Hub natgas expires Monday, Feb 24.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, March finished seven cents lower at $1.64, while deferreds ended down by one to seven cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.4 cents to 28.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 548 lots changed hands, up from Wednesday's total of 149.
